page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B processors operating at 2.7 GHz, it features 16 physical cores and 32 virtual CPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, along with support for AVX-512 and hardware cryptography extensions such as AES and VAES. The system is provisioned with 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a compute-dense memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and operates with a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local SSD storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators are bundled with this server model.

Benchmark evaluations position the performance of this instance in mid-tier brackets across general compute benchmarks, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 34,961.9 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,846.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests recorded 126.91 GB/sec for reads and 58.65 GB/sec for writes. The server demonstrates high throughput in lightweight AI workloads, achieving top-quartile results in small 135M model LLM text generation at 266.46 tokens per second, alongside 28.45 million Redis SET operations per second and 25.39 GB/sec in static web serving tests.

From a resource design perspective, the 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-efficient resource profile for CPU-bound applications that do not demand extensive memory allocations. Because persistent local storage is absent, storage reliance is transferred to attached cloud disk volumes over the 16 Gbps network link. This configuration is well-suited for software compilation, microservices execution, web serving, key-value data caching, and small-scale machine learning inference.
